new_candidates.body:
`SerialMotorsBus.sync_read()` reads Dynamixel motors with Sync Read, which takes one status packet per motor. Protocol 2.0 also has [Fast Sync Read (0x8A)](https://emanual.robotis.com/docs/en/dxl/protocol2/#fast-sync-read-0x8a): all the motors answer in a single status packet, which shortens the reads of a control loop.

rustypot 1.11.0's mixed-model `Bus` does not expose it. Once it does, use it for reads only, not writes, and only on the models and firmware versions that answer it.

Follow-up of the review of #4672, which replaced the Dynamixel SDK (where Fast Sync Read came with release 3.8.2, ROBOTIS-GIT/DynamixelSDK#643) with rustypot.
new_candidates.title: Motors: read Dynamixel motors with Fast Sync Read

new_candidates.body:
`SerialMotorsBus.sync_read()` sends a Sync Read and waits for every answer before it returns. A control loop could instead send the next Sync Read as soon as it has the answers to the previous one, so that the motors answer while the loop computes, and collect those answers at the next tick.

The cost is the age of the observation: the values a tick returns were measured one tick earlier, which adds latency between the moment the motors measure and the moment a policy uses the measure. An implementation has to make that explicit to its callers.

rustypot does not offer this: it would need a way to send a read and collect its answers later. This moves here a TODO that #4672 removed along with the vendor SDKs, as asked in its review.
new_candidates.title: Motors: pipeline the sync read of a control loop

new_candidates.body:
`SerialMotorsBus.read()`, `write()`, `sync_read()` and `sync_write()` take the register as a free string, e.g. `"Present_Position"`, checked only when rustypot looks it up at run time. A typo shows up as a runtime error, on the hardware.

A static check, such as a `Literal` or an enum of the register names, would let mypy catch it. The vendor control tables need not come back: the names can be generated from rustypot's servo definitions.

Follow-up of the review of #4672, which removed the Feetech control tables and their TODO about typed register keys.
new_candidates.title: Motors: check register names statically

new_candidates.body:
### Description



## Description

Starting an otherwise empty, headless Isaac Sim 6.1 `SimulationApp` activates
CUPTI-backed CUDA allocation address tracking during
`omni.kit.renderer.init`. In the same process, this has two observable effects:

1. `torch.profiler` cannot collect CUDA events and reports
   `CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUPPORTED`.
2. PyTorch workloads containing many sequential small CUDA operations become
   materially slower. Recurrent/BPTT training is affected much more than large
   GEMM or convolution workloads.

The reproducer does not create a USD stage, physics scene, sensor, or rendered
frame. Merely constructing `SimulationApp` is sufficient.

The measurements and attached reproducer use
`isaacsim.exp.base.zero_delay.kit` to match the original workload. Extension
bisection localizes the activation boundary to `omni.kit.renderer.init`, so
there is no evidence that the behavior is specific to the zero-delay
experience. Other complete Isaac Sim experiences were not benchmarked.

## Environment

- OS: headless Linux
- Installation: Isaac Sim Python packages
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090
- NVIDIA driver: 580.178.04
- Isaac Sim 5.1.0.0 environment: PyTorch 2.7.0+cu128
- Isaac Sim 6.1.0.0 environment: PyTorch 2.11.0+cu128
- CUDA runtime reported by both PyTorch builds: 12.8

## Minimal reproduction

The attached `repro.py` is self-contained. Run it twice with the Isaac Sim 6.1
Python environment on an otherwise idle GPU.

First, keep the default address-tracking behavior:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /path/to/isaacsim610/bin/python repro.py \
  2>&1 | tee isaacsim610_tracking_default.log
```

Then disable only CUDA allocation-address tracking:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 /path/to/isaacsim610/bin/python repro.py \
  --disable-address-tracking \
  2>&1 | tee isaacsim610_tracking_off.log
```

Each command starts a fresh process and emits one `RESULT_JSON=...` line. No
simulator frame is advanced. The first log preserves the CUPTI diagnostic; the
second run shows whether CUDA profiler events and small-kernel performance are
restored.

For optional controls, run the same script with the Isaac Sim 5.1 Python
environment, or pass `--torch-only` to skip `SimulationApp` initialization.

## Actual behavior

With the default Isaac Sim 6.1 setting, the renderer log reports CUDA memory
tracking activation and PyTorch reports:

```text
CUPTI_ERROR_MULTIPLE_SUBSCRIBERS_NOT_SUPPORTED
```

Repeated medians collected on one otherwise idle GPU were:

| Workload | PyTorch without Isaac Sim | Isaac Sim 6.1 | 6.1 tracking disabled |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 3000 small in-place CUDA kernels | 11.867 ms | 15.331 ms | 13.944 ms |
| 20 large matrix multiplications | 6.374 ms | 6.259 ms | 6.373 ms |

A representative recurrent/BPTT optimizer step measured:

| Runtime | Seconds per optimizer step |
|---|---:|
| Isaac Sim 5.1 | 0.958 s |
| Isaac Sim 6.1 | 1.203 s |
| Isaac Sim 6.1, tracking disabled | 0.973 s |

Disabling address tracking recovered about 94% of the observed 5.1-to-6.1
training-performance gap. The fixed 6.1 result was approximately 1.5% slower
than 5.1 instead of 25.6% slower.

## Isolation results

Extension bisection in a single process localized the activation boundary:

| Initialized components | Forward | Backward |
|---|---:|---:|
| Minimal Kit loop/USD application | 333.323 ms | 448.801 ms |
| Minimal Kit plus `omni.gpu_foundation` | 335.037 ms | 450.983 ms |
| Minimal Kit plus `omni.kit.renderer.init` | 449.693 ms | 640.844 ms |

An idle 6.1 `SimulationApp` in a separate process did not slow the PyTorch
process. This localizes the behavior to process-global instrumentation rather
than GPU capacity, clocks, or cross-process contention.

Disabling Tracy, PerfSDK, renderer GPU-profiler settings, or the top-level
memory-tracking statistic after startup did not release the CUPTI subscriber.

## Workaround

Passing the following Kit setting before constructing `SimulationApp` restores
PyTorch CUDA profiling and nearly all of the recurrent-training performance:

```text
--/plugins/carb.memorytracking.plugin/memoryScope/trackAddress/enabled=false
```

For example:

```python
simulation_app = isaacsim.SimulationApp(
    launch_config={
        "headless": True,
        "extra_args": [
            "--/plugins/carb.memorytracking.plugin/"
            "memoryScope/trackAddress/enabled=false"
        ],
    },
    experience=experience_file,
)
```

The setting must be supplied before `SimulationApp` starts. Changing it after
renderer initialization is too late because the CUPTI subscriber is already
registered.

## Expected behavior

Diagnostic CUDA address tracking should either be disabled by default for
normal headless applications, coexist with other CUPTI consumers, or avoid
adding material overhead to unrelated CUDA workloads. Initializing an idle
`SimulationApp` should not prevent PyTorch CUDA profiling or materially slow
training performed later in the same process.

Could NVIDIA confirm whether this address tracker is expected to be enabled
during normal headless renderer initialization, and whether it can be disabled
by default or exposed as a documented `SimulationApp` option?

## Attachment
Code: 
[repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33421032/repro.py)

### Isaac Sim version

6.1.0

### Operating System (OS)

Ubuntu 24.04

### GPU Name

GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090

### GPU Driver and CUDA versions

580.178.04, CUDA 12.8

### Logs

_No response_

### Additional information

_No response_

new_candidates.body:
Since #1308 (merged 2026-06-10), `Sim2RealEnv` raises `RecursionError` on its first `reset()` whenever the simulation env has a gym wrapper, for example `FlattenRGBDObservationWrapper` (aalmuzairee/squint's `deploy.py` sets it up this way).

**Repro** (ManiSkill only, no robot, CPU, ~10 s):

```python
import gymnasium as gym
import mani_skill.envs
from mani_skill.agents.base_real_agent import BaseRealAgent
from mani_skill.envs.sim2real_env import Sim2RealEnv
from mani_skill.utils.wrappers.flatten import FlattenRGBDObservationWrapper

sim = gym.make("PickCube-v1", obs_mode="rgb", sim_backend="physx_cpu", num_envs=1)
sim = FlattenRGBDObservationWrapper(sim, rgb=True, depth=False, state=True)
real = Sim2RealEnv(sim_env=sim, agent=BaseRealAgent(),
                   real_reset_function=lambda env, seed=None, options=None: None,
                   skip_data_checks=True)
real.reset()  # RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded
```

**Cause.** During `reset()` and `step()`, `Sim2RealEnv` temporarily sets `self._last_wrapper.env` to the `RealEnvStepReset` stand-in, whose `unwrapped` returns the `Sim2RealEnv` itself. Before #1308, `base_sim_env` was an attribute set once in `__init__` (`self.base_sim_env: BaseEnv = sim_env.unwrapped`). #1308 turned it into a property, `cast(BaseEnv, self.sim_env.unwrapped)`, which is resolved again on every access. Inside the swap it resolves to the `Sim2RealEnv`, so `get_obs()` runs `self.base_sim_env.__class__.get_obs(self, ...)`, which is itself. `step()` goes through the same swap.

**Versions.** `mani-skill==3.0.1` and `mani_skill_nightly==2026.4.21.550` still have the `__init__` attribute. `mani_skill_nightly==2026.6.23.446`, `2026.8.2.400` and `main` at 62ff3a5 have the property; the repro above recurses on `2026.8.2.400`. Reproduced with gymnasium 1.4; `Wrapper.unwrapped` is identical in 1.3. Seen on macOS (Python 3.11, CPU); the same traceback was reported on Linux in aalmuzairee/squint#7.

**Suggested fix** (keeps the typed property):

```diff
         self.sim_env = sim_env
+        # resolve once, before reset()/step() swap the last wrapper's env
+        self._base_sim_env = cast(BaseEnv, sim_env.unwrapped)
         self.num_envs = 1
@@
     @property
     def base_sim_env(self) -> BaseEnv:
-        return cast(BaseEnv, self.sim_env.unwrapped)
+        return self._base_sim_env
```

With this the repro no longer recurses (it reaches the stub agent's `capture_sensor_data`, which a real agent implements), and a full SO-101 deploy runs for us. Happy to open a PR with a regression test if this looks right.
new_candidates.title: [Bug] Sim2RealEnv.reset() recurses forever when the sim env is wrapped (regression from #1308)
